To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
human MCPH1-deficiency causes subtle effects on the cellular DNA-damage response that may explain the absence in MCPH1 patients of cancer predisposition.
MCPH1-deficiency in patient-derived cells does not affect the cellular DNA damage responses in a significant manner.
MCPH1-deficiency in humans is associated with a delay in the resolution of DNA damage, and that this delay is not due to a defective DNA damage response.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms of human primary microcephaly.
the molecular and cellular basis of microcephaly and the DNA damage response, two processes that are intimately related.
understanding the cellular phenotype associated with MCPH1 deficiency in human cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MCPH1 deficiency in human cells is not associated with gross defects in the cellular DNA damage repair and checkpoint response.
MCPH1 mutations cause primary microcephalic aneuploidy, and that the DNA damage checkpoint is not affected in these cells.
MCPH1 mutations in human cells cause a delay in the release from DNA damage induced cell cycle checkpoint arrest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
human MCPH1 mutations cause microcephaly and a unique chromosome condensation phenotype, but do not cause a severe DNA damage response phenotype.
MCPH1 deficiency does not affect the G2/M checkpoint, but it may affect mitotic entry.
MCPH1 deficiency does not lead to a global defect in the DNA damage checkpoint response in human cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
MCPH1-deficiency does not cause a grossly defective G2/M checkpoint, but rather a subtle defect in the resolution of the checkpoint arrest.
MCPH1 deficiency does not lead to a severe impairment of the G2/M checkpoint and that MCPH1-deficiency is not associated with a severe defect in the DNA damage signaling cascade.
caution is required when extrapolating results of RNAi-mediated MCPH1 depletion to MCPH1 patient cells, and that MCPH1-deficiency should be investigated in the context of a specific cell type.
